predicate: (phase==0) & isin(t,[2,3]) & isin(prev_tok,[tok("g"),tok("y")]) & isin(in_tok,[tok(c) for c in "bmatjcx10l"]) & isin(orig(0),[tok(c) for c in "gxofq3"])
explanation: Fires only in the original phase, almost all of it at t=2-3 (about 95% of mass; a small tail at t=4-5), and never on the delimiter or copy steps. The strongest cue is the previous input: g or y account for about 89% of mass. Activation is also enriched when the current token is one of b,m,a,t,j,c,x,1,0,l and when the first token is one of g,x,o,f,q,3, and it is mostly on a token appearing for the first time. The top examples look like o g y [b], f g g [a], q g g [b], q g y [a]. So it picks out a specific region of hidden state set up by a short prefix rather than any single variable. prev_tok in {g,y} at t=2-3 covers 85% of mass but has precision 4%. The full five-way conjunction reaches dev F1 0.41 (P 0.34, R 0.52). Magnitude is fairly flat (median 0.12, max 0.22); the top-quartile examples follow the 3-token prefix pattern most cleanly, but I did not model magnitude beyond that.
